chapter: Barnet, 52nd Street and New York recording dates
title: Jimmy Ryan's, Leo Watson and Basie at the Famous Door
summary: Bechet played at Jimmy Ryan's with Vic Dickenson and Leo Watson, and Basie's 14-piece band crammed into the tiny Famous Door.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When did you go there, 4:00 o'clock in the morning then?

Yeah, it went from about 10:00 to 4:00. And Sidney Bechet was down there. He was playing at Jimmy Ryan's then. So all the guys who really played Dixieland music, the top guys were in there. I remember Vic Dickenson was playing in there with him, and Leo Watson was scat singing.
He was fronting the band. Did you ever hear him?
You mentioned Errol Garner was there. How about Linton Garner? Was he there too in New York then too?

No, he wasn't there then. He wasn't there then. He wasn't -- Slam Stewart was down there then, though. He was playing off 52nd Street. And Basie with his big band, he used to work down there at the Famous Door -- how they got them up there, I'll never know, man, but they sure used to rock

that place, man, and they took up half the room. The band took up almost -- those rooms, you got to remember, they never did seat over 75, 80, 85 people, hardly any of those rooms in there, because about a 14 piece band in there, you know, it's some guy -- the piano was down on the floor. You had to have that down there, and you had all the guys -- I guess that's why they sounded good. They all were concentrated right together, like up in a little nook or something like that. And they sounded real good.
